card.name: Verbs completing fixed label phrases
card.fires_on: The key verb or noun that finishes a stock phrase in drug-label text, such as 'a decision should be made' or 'reasonable to expect'. It also fires on a few first pieces of drug names.

modes.label: Stock phrase verb
modes.description: A verb that completes a set regulatory phrase about decisions or expectations.
modes.example: a decision should be<< made>> whether to discontinue nursing or discontinue

modes.label: Start of a drug name
modes.description: An early piece of a drug name, such as the first letters of fluphenazine or venlafaxine.
modes.example: to use of<< Fl>>uphenazine Decanoate Injection;

modes.label: Other idiom ends
modes.description: A noun or verb ending a common phrase such as 'take for granted' or 'any conclusion'.
modes.example: the number is too small to allow any<< conclusion>> about drug effect on suicide.

card.plain: It marks the key word in a standard label phrase, such as 'a decision should be made', where the next words are predictable.
